claims.why: Minted by the debug run that crashed at 14:28 before reaching any sweep. Never presented, so settling burns it and returns ISSUER-A's capacity while paying nobody — the shape a crashed run leaves behind (spec §4.6al). This is the claim that made the 14:46 run start at 70,000 of 80,000 without saying so.

The 14:46 debug run's window-3 claim: presented, never served, and minted in the last window so no later window existed in which its holder could be offered it (§4.6z-ii). The run's own report flagged it under holdersNeverOfferedSettlement. Settling draws on ISSUER-A's bond and pays WORKER-CODE.

method: simulateContract before each send; attestation signed from the real 2026-10-03 commodity print via signRateAttestationForPrint, never assembled by hand.
readingNote: The read taken immediately after the two sends returned 70,000. That was stale — the fifth instance of the pattern in docs/methodology.md. A fresh client at a later block returns 80,000. The rule held; the first figure was not reported as fact.
doNotCountAs: agent behaviour. Neither settlement may appear in any fulfilment, enforcement or holder-responsiveness statistic.
